specification.problem: Approximate a single-qubit z-rotation Rz(theta) to operator-norm precision eps (up to global phase) by an ancilla-free Clifford+T circuit, via a number-theoretic exact synthesis baseline. This is a comparator, not the paper's RUS construction with one ancilla and measurement.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One data qubit, one tiny instance (e.g. theta=pi/8 style small angle with modest eps such as 0.1): sample u in Z[omega] near the scaled target entry, solve the norm equation for t, form the exact unitary, and synthesize it exactly into a Clifford+T word. Outside scope: the RUS circuit, ancilla and measurement, the paper's probabilistically polynomial RUS synthesis algorithm, the 2.5x expected T-count reduction, and the numerical evidence. A ZYZ extension to general U is only described, not built.

symbols.meaning: exact unitary built from (u,t), entries in Z[1/sqrt2,i]
initial computational basis state of the data qubit

equations.label: Target and approximation criterion
equations.description: Target rotation and precision requirement, global phase ignored
equations.abstract_quote: approximate any given single-qubit unitary within precision $\varepsilon$
equations.justification: The abstract states approximation within precision eps; the operator norm is an assumed metric.
assumptions: Operator-norm metric up to global phase

equations.label: Candidate and norm equation
equations.description: Sample u near the scaled target entry and require 2^k-|u|^2 to be a norm from Z[omega] so t exists
equations.justification: Standard number-theoretic approach recalled from background, not stated in the abstract. The plan omitted the sqrt2^k scaling; this is a correction. Here |.|^2 is the complex modulus squared, and for Z[omega] the equation is an exact equality in the real subring.
assumptions: t found by randomized factoring with Miller-Rabin tests and sums of two squares over primes

equations.label: Exact unitary
equations.description: Exact unitary from the solved pair; unitary by the norm equation
equations.justification: Standard form of a Clifford+T-synthesizable matrix; determinant is (|u|^2+|t|^2)/2^k=1.

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Data qubit starts in |0>; the circuit unitary is applied. Equivalent verification uses the full 2x2 unitary.
equations.justification: A fixed input state is needed for implementation. This replaces the equation-specialist's prediction, which was rejected because its state includes an unjustified ancilla and does not follow from the cited relation.

equations.label: T-count reference
equations.description: The abstract's ancilla-free reference bound; the comparator is expected near this order, with unverified O(log log) overhead
equations.abstract_quote: theoretical lower bound of $3\log_{2}(1/\varepsilon)$ for ancilla-free single-qubit circuit decomposition
equations.justification: Stated in the abstract; used only as a reference.

registers.name: q
registers.role: data qubit q0 on which the synthesized Clifford+T unitary acts; the only qubit

specification.initial_state: |0> on the single data qubit q0 (|psi_0> = |0>). The full unitary is compared to the target, so the choice of input state does not affect the check.

steps.description: Fix theta and eps and prepare the data qubit in |0>. For a general U, ZYZ Euler angles would give three z-rotations with H/S conjugation (outside the built scope).
Randomly sample candidate u in Z[omega] in the eps-disc; test solvability of the norm equation for t by randomized factoring; repeat until a solution is found.
Apply Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca exact synthesis to get a Clifford+T word using h, s, t, tdg, x as a measurement-free circuit; compare its T-count to the reference.

specification.measurement: None. The circuit is a measurement-free unitary. Decoding compares the simulated 2x2 unitary to the target up to global phase using operator-norm distance.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical sampling, factoring and exact synthesis produce the gate word; the distance to the target is then evaluated.
assumptions: The ancilla-free number-theoretic baseline is chosen as the smallest implementable construction; it does not reproduce the paper's RUS method.
Metric is the operator norm up to global phase.
Polynomial classical runtime relies on prime density about 1/log, an unverified expectation.
Initial state |0> is a chosen convention.
